checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Same woman at kitchen table throughout
must.why: Same woman, kitchen and framing in all frames.

must.item: Subtitles cover the complete sentence without omissions or inventions
must.why: The 1 s frame shows her speaking with no subtitle, so 'Hi everyone!' appears to be missing. The later words look correct.

must.item: Subtitle chunks appear with the matching speech
must.why: Different chunks show at 4 s and 7 s and match the speech progress. No full transcript is shown at once.

must.item: Readable, inside the frame, not covering face
must.why: Bold white text with black outline sits at the bottom, over her torso and hands, clear of her face and inside the frame.

must.item: Original speech audible and framing preserved
must.why: Framing is preserved and the audio has a -0.6 dB peak, but the speech content can't be verified.

exact_text.read_as: No subtitle at the 1 s frame, while she is visibly speaking.

exact_text.text: Today I want to show you
exact_text.read_as: Today I want to show you three easy
'three easy' then 'ways' in the next chunk

exact_text.text: to make your mornings less stressful.
exact_text.read_as: ways to make your mornings less stressful.

faults.what: The greeting 'Hi everyone!' has no subtitle; the 1 s frame shows her speaking with none visible.
The last subtitle stays on screen at 9.5 s after her speech appears to have ended, so it lingers.
'three easy ways' is split across two subtitle chunks.
The subtitle sits over her torso and hands, which is slightly busy but acceptable.

summary: The clip has readable, well-placed subtitles that follow her speech and keep the framing, but the opening 'Hi everyone!' appears to have no subtitle, and 'three easy ways' is split across chunks.
